strategy.summary: Reproduce PR #21505 by building scipy at the buggy commit 28709e534336 (the parent of the PR) and running the PR's new mpmath-referenced test test_cdflib.py::test_ncfdtr. That test calls sp.ncfdtr on 12 parametrized (dfn,dfd,nc,f) cases and asserts rtol=1e-13 against mpmath values. On the buggy revision ncfdtr is the legacy cdflib Fortran path and at least one case should miss the tolerance; on the fixed revision, where ncfdtr uses the vendored Boost wrapper, all 12 should pass. The environment is an era-matched scipy source build (numpy<=2.1, scipy~1.14 era) with gfortran and a C++ compiler. Boost is the vendored copy in scipy/_lib, so no system Boost is planned. mpmath is only needed to regenerate references, not to run the test.

environment.python_version: 3.11 (era-inferred: scipy 1.14 supports 3.10-3.12; not stated by evidence)
pip_packages: numpy<=2.1 (era ceiling, numerically relevant, not documented)
system_packages: gfortran (cdflib Fortran path is the buggy legacy kernel)
g++ with C++17 support (Boost-wrapped ncfdtr in the fixed revision)
BLAS/LAPACK dev package (e.g. libopenblas-dev) as scipy build requires
build_commands: git checkout 28709e534336 (buggy revision) then apply the PR test diff for scipy/special/tests/test_cdflib.py only
python -m pip install -r requirements/build.txt (or equivalent) then python dev.py build, or pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
run the test from the built tree (dev.py test or pytest against the in-tree build)
repeat on the fixed (PR merge) revision for the pass side, keeping the same build flags
pinned_because: numpy <=2.1: era ceiling at PR date 2024-09-07, numerically relevant per evidence but not documented
scipy checkout at 28709e534336: the revision under test; version string in issue #8344 is historical only and not used
boost: NOT pinned. Chosen to be the Boost vendored in scipy/_lib at the checked-out commit, since the evidence gives no version and the fixed code uses that vendored wrapper
mpmath: NOT pinned. Not needed to run the test; reference values are hard-coded in the test and mpmath only appears in the regeneration script comment

strategy.test_command: python dev.py test -t scipy.special.tests.test_cdflib::test_ncfdtr (equivalently: pytest scipy/special/tests/test_cdflib.py -k test_ncfdtr -v)
strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/special/tests/test_cdflib.py::test_ncfdtr, parametrized over 12 (dfn,dfd,nc,f,expected) tuples, asserting assert_allclose(sp.ncfdtr(dfn,dfd,nc,f), expected, rtol=1e-13, atol=0)
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision (cdflib ncfdtr), test_cdflib.py::test_ncfdtr FAILS because at least one of the 12 parametrized cases misses rtol=1e-13 against the mpmath reference. On the fixed revision (Boost ncfdtr), all 12 parametrized cases PASS. The xfail markers added to test_basic.py ncfdtri/ncfdtridfd/ncfdtridfn/ncfdtrinc tests are not part of the transition and only need to not error.
strategy.numerical_probe: sp.ncfdtr(6, 33, 30.4, 20) should be approximately 0.9989 (cross-check against R/Matlab 0.998921); use only as a sanity check, not as the pass/fail criterion, since the R/Matlab value has about six digits and the test's 1e-13 tolerance is the real gate
risks: The fail side depends on the buggy cdflib ncfdtr producing an error above 1e-13 on at least one of the 12 cases; the evidence does not give the buggy per-case values, so which case fails is unverified until the run.
Boost is unbounded in the evidence. The plan relies on the vendored Boost at the commit, which is an era-inferred choice, not a documented constraint.

The 0.998868 vs 0.998921 discrepancy is in stats.ncf.cdf; the evidence does not say whether scipy.special.ncfdtr or the stats wrapper produced it. The target test calls scipy.special directly, so the stats path is not what is being reproduced.

Behaviour may depend on platform: the cdflib error and the Boost result are both floating-point sensitive, and the evidence names no architecture. If the buggy error is only seen on one architecture or with a specific compiler/optimization level, the fail side may not transition on x86_64 Linux with a different compiler. Record the platform and compiler used.
Sanitizer or debug builds are not planned; a defect visible only under sanitizers would not transition in a normal build.
nc domain was widened from (0,1e4) to [0,inf); the 12 test cases use nc<=100 so this should not matter, but avoid inputs above 1e4.
Issue #8344 concerns nctdtr (cumtnc.f), not ncfdtr; do not assume its reproduction applies.
The test_basic.py xfail markers are strict-free by default; if the Boost path makes the inverse tests pass, they XPASS and do not fail the run, so they are not part of the transition.
The test_distributions.py change removes a 32-bit skipif; the target test is not 32-bit specific, but a 32-bit build would be a different environment and is not planned.

oracle.reference_source: mpmath with mp.dps=100 using formula 26.2.20 from Abramowitz and Stegun (script in test comment)
oracle.why: The test hard-codes mpmath values and compares with rtol 1e-13; the tolerance is stated in the test itself, so it is grounded rather than invented. The R/Matlab reference 0.998921 is only about 6 digits and is used as a cross-check.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision sp.ncfdtr dispatches to the legacy cdflib implementation. assert_allclose(..., rtol=1e-13, atol=0) compares its array output with the mpmath expected array, and at least one parametrized case exceeds the 1e-13 relative error, so the test reports a failure.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision sp.ncfdtr uses the Boost wrapper and every one of the 12 parametrized cases matches the mpmath reference within rtol=1e-13, so the test passes.
